title: tiered-commit-window-and-graceful-preempt-reserve-controller
author: Priya Kaur
release_notes: Introduces a tiered commit/reserve controller to reduce noisy preemptions and improve sustained throughput across Dedicated fleets. Backwards-compatible defaults; ops can tune reserve windows per-tier.
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets saw periodic noisy preemptions during short-lived demand spikes which caused tail latency regressions for pinned workloads. This PR implements a tiered commit window and a graceful preempt reserve controller that reduces premature preemption while preserving capacity elasticity. Summary: add a new controller (pkg/fleet/preempt_reserve_controller.go) that maintains per-tenant tiered commit windows and a soft reserve ledger. The default policy creates three tiers (burst, sustained, committed) with decaying reserve weights. Additions to the autoscaler allow the scale decision to consult the reserve ledger and favor graceful shrinkage over immediate slot reclamation. Telemetry: new metrics exported under telemetry/fleet_reserve.md including histograms for reserve_utilization_seconds, gauge for tiered_reserve_bytes, and a counter for graceful_preempt_events. Config and ops: charts/dedicated/values.yaml exposes reserve window knobs and rollout safety flags. Tests: unit tests for the ledger and decision policy plus an e2e test (tests/e2e/preempt_reserve_test.go) that validates no-regressive tail latency under synthetic microbursts. Commits: a) feat(reserve): add preempt reserve controller and ledger b) feat(autoscaler): consult reserve ledger in scale-down decision c) perf: reduce lock contention in ledger updates d) docs: operations guide and config knobs e) test: add unit and e2e tests f) ci: flake fixes and test orchestration tweaks. Files changed (high level): pkg/fleet/preempt_reserve_controller.go, pkg/autoscaler/decision.go, pkg/allocator/slotmanager.go, charts/dedicated/values.yaml, telemetry/fleet_reserve.md, docs/ops/preemption.md, tests/unit/ledger_test.go, tests/e2e/preempt_reserve_test.go, scripts/ci/orchestrate_tests.sh, examples/dedicated/commit-policy.yaml, Makefile. Review thread: initial review by Samir requested lowering the default conservative reserve from 25% to 12% and adding a short-circuit for tenants with hard SLAs; implemented in second commit. Anya asked for clearer invariants around ledgers during partial failures; added stronger invariants and an extra integration test that simulates controller restarts. Miguel flagged a potential CPU hotspot in the ledger update path; resolved by moving to per-shard update queues and adding benchmarks. CI notes: first CI run failed due to a flaky e2e harness timeout; timeout increased and harness resilience improved, subsequent runs passed. Performance results: internal canary showed 18% reduction in scale-down-induced tail latencies for affected tenants and a 5% reduction in unnecessary preempt events during 30s microbursts. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves current autoscaler semantics unless the reserve controller is enabled via charts values. Rollout plan: staged rollout with canary on 10% of fleets then 50% then full, with automatic rollback on increased tail latency. Merge: squashed and merged after approvals and green CI. Related work: follows up on ENG-1284 (surge smoothing prototype) and complements pr-309452 probing provision controller. Notes for operators: tune tier windows and reserve weights based on workload burstiness; use provided dashboards to inspect reserve_utilization_seconds histogram when debugging preempt patterns.
